transcript: Last night, I saw The Fires at Soho Rep, a new play written and directed by Raja Feather Kelly. We see three interwoven stories about three different men who lived in the same apartment at different times, but we see their stories playing out simultaneously. To me, this play was about black queer love, the pain and the beauties of its hidden existence, and the similarities and differences across generations in navigating it. The intergenerational component of this piece is essential to its structure and themes and I found the broad range of characters fascinating, especially considering the fact that they inhabit the same physical space in the play simultaneously, but not actually at the same time period. This took some getting used to as an audience member. Sometimes it was paramount in illuminating connections and allowing different scenes to speak with one another while other times it was straight up distracting. Some of the more surreal lighting and sound elements also didn't quite click for me and felt a bit disjointed, but overall I thought the direction and the writing aligned for me and I thought the piece was very successful in painting a sprawling portrait of queer love, and in it, the dichotomy between the personal and the universal. With that, other program for my collection.
